text:
alex chan: Quick heads-up — canary with microbatch=8 + token_chunk=16 shows an awkward UX regression: p95 improved but short responses feel slower (p50 up). attaching the short dump i grabbed.

maria g: Paste the numbers & kernel trace? curious if kernel switch or KV-cache misses.

alex chan: sure — short paste from test run (tail of profiler):
```
req_type=chat, avg_seq=24
microbatch=1->8 (canary)
metrics_before(mb=1): p50=72ms, p95=540ms, p99=720ms
metrics_after(mb=8):  p50=140ms, p95=410ms, p99=670ms
kernel_log: chosen_kernel=int8_gemm_v2 if seq_len>=64 else f32_tile_opt
kv_cache: hit_ratio=0.62 (was 0.78 before)
flush_intervals_ms=30 (token_chunk=16 -> flush every ~30ms when streaming)
```

sven r: interesting — p95 drop means batching is amortizing overhead, but p50 jump + lower kv hit ratio suggests the per-request path changed (more initial warm compute + serialization). could be microbatch packing delaying first token emission.

lucy: yes — with microbatch=8 we wait to fill batch or to reach flush timer. token_chunk=16 means we buffer more tokens before emitting, which hurts perceived latency for short replies.

maria g: did the kernel selection change for short seqs? f32_tile_opt might be slower on short lengths if it's doing extra packing. is there a log that shows per-request kernel decision + decision timestamp?

alex chan: i pulled a per-request trace for a 12-token reply:
```
[req id=abc123] arrival=0ms
select_kernel start=2ms -> selected=f32_tile_opt (decision cost ~1.4ms)
kv lookup start=3ms -> miss (fallback compute), kv populate end=120ms
emit first token start=125ms
batch drain wait ~ (microbatch wait) = 18ms extra
```

alex chan: so two contributors: f32 kernel path + KV miss + microbatch wait -> first token out at ~125+18ms = ~143ms which matches p50.

sven r: ok. quick ideas: (1) lower token_chunk to 4 or 2 for streaming short replies, (2) reduce initial microbatch target for low-token requests (adaptive microbatching), (3) prefer low-overhead kernel for seq<32 (force int8_gemm or a shallow path).

lucy: +1 for adaptive: emit first token immediately with a super-low flush (8ms) and then let microbatching kick in for subsequent tokens. that usually preserves perceived latency while keeping throughput. we call it "first-token fastpath".

maria g: can we do an A/B: variant A = microbatch=8 + token_chunk=16 (current), variant B = microbatch=8 + token_chunk=4 + first-token-fastpath enabled. run 1h sweep on low-latency chat traces and compare p50/p95 + tokens/hr.

perf-bot: perf-smoke summary (last run):
- variant A (canary): p50=140ms, p95=410ms, tokens/s=1200
- variant B (local tweak): p50=78ms, p95=430ms, tokens/s=1150
- delta: p50 -44%, p95 +5%, throughput -4%

alex chan: that looks promising — perceived latency better, small p95 regression but within SLO? we need product signoff if p95 increase visible.

sven r: for safety we can also add a kernel hint: prefer fwd-light kernel for seq<32 (zero-alloc path). that should shave off ~10-20ms. i'll prototype a gateswitch in runtime.

lucy: also KV policy: increase prefetched prefix caching TTL for short chat sessions — kv hit goes up -> less re-compute. but careful with memory. maybe LRU per-connection cap.

maria g: action items:
- sven: prototype kernel hint gate for short seq (PR + perf bench) — ETA EOD tomorrow
- lucy: implement first-token-fastpath + token_chunk=4 AB test config (run 1h by EOD)
- alex: collect example traces showing UX diffs for product review (short videos/screenshots)
- perf-bot: run ab test and post metrics summary in this thread when done

alex chan: thanks — feel free to ping if you need buckets or test harness tweaks. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: AB test queued (id=ab-2026-03-18-04). will post results when complete.
